headline: Every segment grows as trading and dealmaking fees surge
summary_short: Revenue rose 15% y/y to $31.6 billion and net income climbed 27% to $9.1 billion, with diluted EPS up 34% to $1.21 as investment banking fees jumped 50% and sales-and-trading revenue rose 33%.
summary_long: Growth was broad-based: NII rose 9% to $16.0 billion on higher trading-related NII and loan and deposit growth; sales-and-trading revenue rose 33% to $7.1 billion (equities +70%, FICC +9%); investment banking fees jumped 50% to $2.1 billion. Provision for credit losses fell to $1.4 billion with the net charge-off ratio improving to 0.47%. Noninterest expense rose 8% to $18.6 billion, but the efficiency ratio improved 359bp to 59%, producing 6.6% operating leverage. CET1 capital rose to $201.6 billion (11.2% ratio, Standardized). The company returned $8.0 billion to shareholders — $2.0 billion in dividends, $6.0 billion in buybacks. No numeric forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: CEO Moynihan called it 'one of our strongest quarters,' citing double-digit net income growth in every segment; CFO Borthwick cited disciplined execution and a $3.5 trillion balance sheet as sources of strength.
Release attributes the 15% y/y increase to higher net interest income, sales-and-trading revenue, asset management fees and investment banking fees.
Net income growth outpaced revenue growth as an 8% rise in noninterest expense was more than offset by higher revenue and a lower year-over-year credit-loss provision.
EPS growth of 34% y/y reflects higher net income combined with a 4.7% reduction in weighted diluted shares from buybacks.
Share count fell as the company repurchased $6.0 billion of common stock in the quarter, part of $8.0 billion returned to shareholders.
